title: Spring & Simple Harmonic Motion (Resonance)
description: Investigate Hooke's law, mass-spring harmonic oscillation, natural frequencies, damping regimes, and mechanical resonance

variables.massDesc: Mass attached to the end of the spring in kilograms
variables.kDesc: Stiffness rating and restoring force per unit length in N/m
variables.initialXDesc: Initial stretch or compression from equilibrium position
variables.dampingDesc: Fluid viscosity and friction dissipating kinetic energy
variables.driveAmpDesc: External periodic driving force applied to study resonance
variables.driveFreqDesc: Frequency of external harmonic driver in Hertz

presets.undampedSimpleDesc: Ideal frictionless oscillation with constant amplitude and mechanical energy conservation
presets.underdampedDesc: Exponential amplitude envelope decay due to viscous drag in real mode
presets.resonanceDesc: Matching driving frequency to natural frequency causing massive amplitude amplification
presets.criticalDesc: Fastest return to equilibrium without oscillating

formulas.hookeLaw: Hooke's law for elastic spring restoring force
formulas.periodFormula: Natural period and angular frequency of a mass-spring system
formulas.resonanceEq: Steady-state amplitude response curve for driven harmonic oscillator

realMode.dampingLoss: Mechanical energy dissipation into thermal heat via viscous fluid resistance

guided.step1Title: Step 1: Verify Mass and Stiffness Dependence
guided.step1Desc: Run with default values. Notice how increasing mass lengthens period T₀ while increasing k shortens it.
guided.step2Desc: Select 'Underdamped Decay'. Observe how the oscillation envelope decays according to e^(-γt).
guided.step3Desc: Select 'Resonance Peak'. Because f_drive matches f₀ = 1.0 Hz, watch the mass build up large amplitude.
